strengths: Significance: The paper targets an increasingly relevant bottleneck: after DiT acceleration, VAE decoding reaches 31.6–40.9% of end-to-end latency in the evaluated pipelines. A faster drop-in decoder would therefore have clear practical value.

Soundness: The proposed combination of channel selection, retained-channel enhancement, topology-preserving shortcut projections, stage-dependent operator replacement, and feature distillation is technically plausible and reasonably motivated by the SVD and latency analyses.

Evaluation breadth is a merit. Results cover two substantially different VAE backbones, RTX 5090D and Jetson Orin hardware, UCF-101 reconstruction, 720p DAVIS transfer, temporal consistency, and three accelerated generation pipelines.

The reported efficiency improvements are substantial: approximately 5.6–6.2x decoding speedups in the main comparisons, up to 27–36% end-to-end pipeline speedups, fewer parameters, and markedly lower peak VRAM. Flash-VAED also consistently improves quality over the matched LightVAE/Turbo-VAED baselines.

The ablations provide useful evidence for pruning ratio, channel-selection method, distillation placement, and projection initialization. The appendix also reports scaling with resolution and sequence length and identifies concrete failure cases.
Presentation is generally clear and visually polished. The paper includes a limitations section, and the work presents no evident major ethical risk.
weaknesses: Soundness: The strongest claims are overstated. On Wan, PSNR falls from 40.40 to 37.61 dB and LPIPS worsens from 0.0190 to 0.0285; on 720p DAVIS, LPIPS worsens from 0.0487 to 0.0769. These are not obviously “negligible” losses, particularly because PSNR is logarithmic. Reporting “93.1%” or “96.9%” quality by dividing PSNR values in dB is not a meaningful quality-retention measure.

The claimed “full” or “strict” latent-distribution alignment is not established. Figure 10 is an unexplained two-dimensional visualization with no projection method, sample count, or quantitative distribution distance, and a decoder consumes rather than defines the input latent distribution. Similar reconstruction and VBench scores support compatibility, but not the stronger distributional claim.

The “universal” and broad architectural-generalization claims exceed the evidence. Full quality results are provided only for two convolutional decoders. HunyuanVideo and CogVideoX receive only selected-layer SVD and partial operator-speed analyses, while transformer-based VAEs are discussed speculatively.

The experimental protocol omits important information: reconstruction and VBench sample counts, repeated-run variance or confidence intervals, latency warm-up and timing procedures, precision, batch size, compilation settings, and Jetson power mode. Exact VBench values are mostly shown only as radar plots, making small claimed differences difficult to assess.

Reproducibility is incomplete despite considerable implementation detail. The manuscript does not specify phase-wise training schedules, distilled layer sets, calibration data and tensor construction for SVD/greedy selection, stopping criteria, or sufficient details to reproduce the pruning algorithm. The stated code availability is not accompanied by an accessible artifact in the manuscript.

The ablation study does not fully isolate the complete method. There is no clear factorial comparison of operator optimization, channel pruning, retained-channel enhancement, and all three training phases under matched compute; Table 7 isolates only parameters and memory rather than reconstruction quality and latency together.

Baseline coverage and fairness are limited. Each backbone is compared with only one accelerated baseline, the generation evaluation is effectively Wan-centric, and the appendix notes a VAE substitution used in a qualitative FastVideo comparison but not in quantitative evaluation. Training budgets or retuning effort for baselines are not documented.

The temporal metric uses ground-truth optical flow without describing occlusion handling and conflates reconstruction error with temporal instability. Generation evidence also lacks human evaluation despite perceptual fidelity being central to the claims.

Originality is moderate rather than high: channel pruning, least-squares reconstruction, depthwise separable convolution, 3D-to-2D replacement, and feature distillation are established techniques. Their stage-wise integration for video VAE decoders is useful engineering, but the paper does not yet demonstrate a broadly new principle.

The limitations discussion appropriately identifies difficult motion and facial-detail cases, but the impact statement is perfunctory and does not discuss dataset licensing/privacy, use of generated prompts, or the environmental cost of roughly 300 GPU-hours. These are minor ethical-reporting omissions rather than material ethical concerns.

strengths: Significance: Accelerating video VAE decoding is practically relevant, particularly for few-step generation pipelines where Table 9 shows decoding growing from 2.3% to roughly 32–41% of total latency.

Soundness: The manuscript reports substantial measured acceleration on two distinct decoder families and two hardware classes. The strongest results are approximately 5.6–6.2× decoder speedups, complemented by parameter, memory, resolution, and sequence-length analyses.

Evaluation breadth: Reconstruction is assessed with PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and warping error; deployment is demonstrated in Self Forcing, FastVideo, and Causal Forcing pipelines; and the appendix adds 720p DAVIS results.

Presentation: The overall architecture and three-phase training procedure are organized clearly, and the paper includes useful qualitative comparisons and several ablations. The limitations section appropriately acknowledges failures on small fast-moving objects and dense faces.

Originality: The individual ingredients are familiar, but their stage-dependent combination—3D depthwise separation in early stages, 2D operators and channel pruning in later stages, and feature distillation—forms a coherent practical system. weaknesses: Soundness: The headline claims of retaining 93.1% and 96.9% of quality are obtained by dividing PSNR values measured in decibels. Such ratios are not meaningful because PSNR is logarithmic. The Wan result drops from 40.40 to 37.61 dB, corresponding to roughly 90% greater reconstruction MSE, which is difficult to characterize as negligible without perceptual or human evidence.

Soundness: The claimed “full alignment with the original latent distribution” is conceptually unclear. A replacement decoder consumes the same upstream latent rather than determining its distribution. Figure 10 provides unlabeled point clouds with no definition of the represented features, embedding procedure, distance statistic, sample count, or uncertainty, yet the text claims that distributions “perfectly overlap.” Generation results demonstrate compatibility, but not distributional equality.

Soundness: The evidence for the pruning mechanism is too limited for the broad conclusions. The principal SVD plot concerns one 96-channel feature representation, while the method prunes many layers to 12.5–25%. It is not established that the rank observation holds across layers, inputs, timesteps, datasets, or both primary architectures. Appendix results for additional backbones inspect only randomly sampled layers and do not train or evaluate complete Flash-VAED models.

Soundness: Important ablations are missing. The paper does not report a complete quality–latency factorial comparison of channel pruning, operator replacement, retained-channel enhancement, shortcut injection, and the three training phases. Table 7 isolates parameter and memory effects but omits reconstruction quality and latency, while Table 5 does not isolate each proposed phase. Consequently, the contribution of each claimed innovation is uncertain.

Evaluation: Sample counts, uncertainty estimates, repetitions, and significance tests are absent throughout. VBench results for the two main generation pipelines are shown only as radar plots without numerical tables, prompt counts, variance, or benchmark protocol details. Appendix B.3 reports only “randomly selected” VBench dimensions, leaving substantial room for selective reporting.

Evaluation: The temporal metric uses ground-truth optical flow and measures reconstruction discrepancy after warping, but does not specify occlusion masks or flow-validity handling and can largely reflect spatial reconstruction error. No complementary temporal perceptual metric or human evaluation substantiates the claim of negligible temporal degradation.

Reproducibility: The code statement ends with a blank URL. Essential details are also missing, including batch size, duration and schedule of each training phase, channel-selection algorithm pseudocode and computational procedure, how features are sampled to estimate SVD/R²/W, benchmark clip counts, numerical precision, FPS definition, warm-up and timing protocol, and software versions. The curated latent-video pairs and GPT-4o prompt set are not made available or specified sufficiently for reconstruction.

Originality: Most technical components—least-squares reconstruction-based channel selection, depthwise-separable convolution, replacement of 3D by 2D convolution, and feature distillation—are established ideas. The manuscript does not sharply distinguish the channel-selection method from prior reconstruction-based pruning such as ThiNet, so the novelty appears primarily integrative and heuristic.

Presentation: Several statements overreach the evidence, including “universal,” “strict/full alignment,” “perfectly overlaps,” and “outperforms all baselines in both speed and quality.” The method does lose appreciable quality relative to the original decoders, and the claimed architectural generalization to transformer VAEs is only speculative.

Ethics and limitations: The failure-case discussion is useful, but the generic impact statement does not address foreseeable misuse from cheaper video generation, deepfake risks, dataset and generated-prompt provenance, licensing, or the environmental implications of approximately 300 GPU-hours of training. These omissions are not necessarily disqualifying alone but weaken the responsible-research treatment.

strengths: Soundness: The central efficiency result is supported across two substantially different VAE backbones and two hardware classes. Flash-VAED achieves 5.63–6.16× speedups over the original decoders and improves both speed and reconstruction quality over the corresponding accelerated baselines.

Evaluation breadth: The paper reports PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, temporal warping error, FPS, peak memory, parameter count, and end-to-end generation latency. It also evaluates UCF-101, 720p DAVIS videos, multiple frame counts and resolutions, and three generation pipelines.

Methodology: The combination of independence-aware channel selection, topology-preserving shortcut projections, stage-specific operator replacement, and phased distillation is coherent. Ablations support the channel-selection criterion, pruning ratio, projection initialization, and distillation design.

Significance: Accelerating VAE decoding is increasingly useful as denoising becomes faster. The reported 27–36% end-to-end improvements in accelerated generation pipelines make the contribution practically meaningful.

Originality and presentation: Although several ingredients are established techniques, their decoder-specific analysis and integration are reasonably novel. The manuscript is generally clear, well organized, and visually effective, and it includes an honest discussion of failure cases involving small fast-moving objects and faces.
weaknesses: Soundness: Claims of “full alignment,” “strict alignment,” and a “universal” framework are stronger than the evidence. Figure 10 is an underspecified distribution visualization without axes, distance measures, or methodology, while complete implementations are demonstrated only for Wan and LTX-Video. Results for HunyuanVideo and CogVideoX are limited to partial architectural analyses.

The claimed quality retention percentages are computed from PSNR values expressed in decibels, for which percentage ratios are not meaningful. Moreover, some absolute degradation is non-negligible: Wan drops from 40.40 to 37.61 dB and LPIPS rises from 0.0190 to 0.0285; DAVIS shows similarly material gaps. Descriptions such as “negligible quality drops” should therefore be moderated.

Reproducibility is inadequate. The code-availability sentence contains no link, and the manuscript omits evaluation sample counts, preprocessing details, batch size, precision, timing warm-up and synchronization procedures, random seeds, variance across runs, phase-specific training schedules, and sufficient layer-level architecture specifications.

The generation evaluation is difficult to audit: Figure 9 provides radar plots rather than numerical scores, with no uncertainty or number of generated samples. Appendix Table 8 reports only “randomly selected” VBench dimensions, which risks selective reporting. Full per-dimension results and the standard VBench protocol are needed.

The SVD evidence motivating pruning is narrow and underspecified: the sampling procedure, number of videos or activations, and robustness across layers and data distributions are not reported. Likewise, details needed to reproduce greedy channel selection and estimation of the least-squares mappings are missing.

Some ablations confound components or remain unclear. For example, the pruning-ratio table does not clearly state which operator optimizations and training stages are held fixed, and there is no complete factorial ablation separating operator replacement, channel pruning, and distillation in both quality and latency.

Originality is moderate rather than exceptional: depthwise separable convolution, replacement of temporal convolution with 2D convolution, greedy regression-based pruning, and feature distillation are established ideas. The main novelty lies in their adaptation and combination for video VAE decoders.

The ethics discussion is boilerplate. Given that the work lowers the cost of video generation, it should briefly address potential misuse and environmental effects alongside the positive reduction in inference resources.
